note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for rising PSA trend and PI-RADS 3 MRI finding following a previously negative biopsy.

Recently retired mechanical engineer, widowed, living alone. Long-standing hypertension and type 2 diabetes, managed with amlodipine, lisinopril, metoprolol, and empagliflozin. Osteoarthritis and BPH contribute to moderate LUTS (IPSS 11). Ex-smoker (36 pack-years, quit 2021) with known COPD, recently reviewed with pulmonary function testing. Engages in swimming once weekly. PSA has risen steadily from 1.4 ng/mL in Jan 2023 to 3.4 ng/mL in Jan 2025. Prior biopsy in Jan 2023 was negative. Patient reports no haematuria, bone pain, or unexplained weight loss. Physiotherapy for lower back osteoarthritis completed recently.

On DRE, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged, smooth, and non-tender, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals stable vital signs, clear lungs, and no peripheral edema. Abdominal examination is benign with no palpable masses.
